content.body:
The Blitzkrieg revealed that the German Army had spent much the interwar years developing novel ways of fighting war, one of them being the close cooperation between ground and air forces. The converse of this was that the Wehrmacht was acutely aware of how vulnerable ground troops were to air attack. Designed by Rheinmetall, the 20mm FlaK30 initially entered production for the Kriegsmarine in 1934 and was not accepted for service by the Luftwaffe until 1935. The FlaK.30 design was that of an oversized machine gun operating with an open bolt - it was in fact a direct descendant of the MG.30 machinegun. Designed to provide immediate antiaircraft fire against low-flying attack aircraft, its utility as a heavy infantry support weapon was enhanced by 20mm AP ammunition. The FlaK.30 was the most widely used 20mm anti-aircraft weapon in the world by 1940. This light weight weapon, hampered only by a low rate of fire, saw service throughout the entire war on all fronts where Germany fought.
In Battleground Europe you should deploy this gun to provide a close-in anti-aircraft umbrella over attacking forces; try to set up in a brush line or trees behind your main advance, where your HE firepower will not only be useful against enemy aircraft, but can also provide heavy fire support for your advancing infantry as well as a defense against light AFV's. It is a slow to limber/unlimber, so it is a good idea to restrict your fire to limit the ability of roaming enemy infantry or vehicles to find you.
The low rate of fire means that you need to save your ammo to concentrate on hitting low angle-off targets. Clip reload is also slow, keep careful track of your ammunition status so you do not find yourself facing down an enemy tactical bomber with nothing to shoot.
